newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks fall on rate worries in morning.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks fall on rate worries in morning.

text.p: Interest rate jitters kept Hong Kong stocks under pressure in morning trade on Wednesday after a strong report on the U.S. housing market overnight prompted a decline in U.S. bonds and stocks.
The Hang Seng Index was down 92.30 points, or 0.72 percent, at 12,656.61. Turnover was HK$2.23 billion after the first hour of trade.
"Sentiment for the last week has been not really been good," said Michael Ng, a financial analyst at Taiwan Securities.
He said after a strong run early this year the index was vulnerable to any worries about interest rates.
Inflation fears were reignited on Wall Street overnight following a report that new home building in the United States had surged at the fastest pace in nearly three years in February.
The Dow industrials fell 58.92 points to 6,896.56 and the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond fell 2/32 to yield 6.96 percent.
The U.S. Federal Reserve is due to meet on March 25 to deliberate interest rates.
Property stocks led the morning's decline.
"They are still under pressure because we still think the government is trying to cool down the property market," said Rory McAllister at HSBC James Capel.
Shares in Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd fell HK$0.75 to HK$69.25 and Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd was off HK$0.75 at HK$83.50.
Henderson Land Development Co Ltd was steady at HK$64.50. The property developer is due to report its interim results later on Wednesday and analysts expect strong net profit growth.
Kwong Hing International Holdings Ltd, a maker of knitted fabrics, made its market debut on Wednesday.
The stock opened at HK$1.50 compared with an issue price of HK$1.20 but profit-taking emerged later and the shares pared their gains to trade at HK$1.45.
HSBC Holdings plc was down HK$1.00 at HK$181.50 but Hang Seng Bank Ltd rose HK$0.25 to HK$82.75.
March Hang Seng Index futures fell 13 points to 12,672.
